cards.when: 처음 이야기에 올리는 사람 · 물건
cards.en: There is a cat over there.

cards.when: 눈앞에서 일어난 일
cards.en: Wow, it is snowing!

cards.when: 누가 했는지가 새 정보
cards.en: Who came? Minsu did.

cards.when: 「-아서/어서」 앞 문장의 주어
cards.en: I was late because it rained.

cards.when: 이 두 말 앞의 말에는 이/가
cards.en: I am not a doctor. / I want to become a doctor.

split.en: There is a student over there.
Oh, it is raining!
Jiyoung came.
The road is slippery because it snowed.
split.note: 한 문장에 조사가 둘이면 조사 블록도 둘

choose.en: There is a cat over there.
choose.why: 고양이 ends in a vowel, so 가.

choose.en: Who came? Minsu did.
choose.why: 수 ends in a vowel, so 가.

choose.en: I am not a doctor.
choose.why: 아니다 needs 이/가 before it, and 사 is a vowel, so 가.

choose.en: The sky is blue. The clouds are white.
choose.why: 하늘 and 구름 both end in a consonant, so 이 · 이.

fill.en: I was glad because a friend came.

cards.when: 무엇에 대해 이야기할지 화제를 꺼낼 때
cards.en: I am Sujin.

cards.when: 둘을 서로 견주어 다름을 나타낼 때
cards.en: Apples are sweet, but lemons are sour.

cards.when: 세상 누구나 아는 성질이나 사실을 말할 때
cards.en: Cheetahs are fast.

cards.when: 다른 것은 몰라도 이것만큼은 그렇다고 할 때
cards.en: Today at least, I am busy.

split.en: Minsu is tall.
My older sister is a student.
This bag is really heavy.
My younger sibling is kind.

choose.en: The teacher is kind.
choose.why: 선생님 ends in a consonant, so 은.

choose.q: 지영 씨는 무엇을 해요? 저___ 책을 읽어요.
choose.en: What does Jiyoung do? As for me, I read a book.
choose.why: 저 ends in a vowel, so 는.

choose.en: Winter is cold, but summer is hot.
choose.why: Contrasting winter with summer requires the topic marker 은.

choose.en: Watermelons are big, but grapes are small.
choose.why: 수박 ends in a consonant (은) and 포도 ends in a vowel (는).

cards.when: 무엇을 하는지 동작이 닿는 대상을 밝힐 때
cards.en: I drink water every morning.

cards.when: 좋아하거나 싫어하는 대상을 말할 때
cards.en: I like apples.

cards.when: 무엇을 배우거나 읽는지 나타낼 때
cards.en: Jiyoung learns Korean.

cards.when: 물건을 사거나 팔 때
cards.en: I bought bread at the store.

split.en: Minsu writes a letter.
I eat breakfast.
My friend watches a movie.
I read books diligently.

choose.en: I drink milk.
choose.why: 우유 ends in a vowel, so 를.

choose.en: What do you eat? I eat rice.
choose.why: 밥 ends in a consonant, so 을.

choose.en: Minsu washes the apple.
choose.why: 사과 is the object being washed, so 를.

choose.q: 지영이는 신문___ 읽고 민수는 차___ 마셔요.
choose.en: Jiyoung reads the newspaper, and Minsu drinks tea.
choose.why: 신문 ends in a consonant (을) and 차 ends in a vowel (를).

cards.when: 누구의 물건인지 소유를 나타낼 때
cards.en: This is Minsu's bag.

cards.when: 가족이나 친구 사이의 관계를 말할 때
cards.en: Jiyoung's younger sibling is cute.

cards.when: 어느 곳에 속해 있는지 나타낼 때
cards.en: The number of students at our school is large.

cards.when: 고유한 특성이나 배경을 꾸밀 때
cards.en: Korea's autumn sky is high.

split.en: Here is my friend's house.
My mother's glasses are clean.
I read teacher's letter.
Sujin's shoes are white.

choose.en: These are mother's clothes.
choose.why: Showing possession 'mother's' takes the possessive marker 의.

choose.en: Whose umbrella is it? It is Minsu's umbrella.
choose.why: Answering whose umbrella it is requires the possessive marker 의.

choose.en: My younger sibling's hat is really pretty.
choose.why: Modifying the hat belonging to sibling takes 의.

choose.en: My friend's name is Sujin.
choose.why: 'Friend's name' uses 의, and 이름 as the topic takes 은.

cards.when: 사람이나 사물이 어디에 있는지 말할 때 (있다/없다)
cards.en: There is a book on the desk.

cards.when: 살다, 머물다와 함께 머무르는 장소를 나타낼 때
cards.en: My family lives in Seoul.

cards.when: 몇 시, 무슨 요일 등 일이 일어나는 시간을 가리킬 때
cards.en: I wake up at seven in the morning.

cards.when: 주말이나 특정 날짜를 지정할 때
cards.en: Let's meet on Saturday.

split.en: My friend is in the room.
There are no apples in the refrigerator.
I eat lunch at twelve o'clock.
My younger sibling sleeps at night.

choose.en: The teacher is in the classroom.
choose.why: Indicating static location with 계시다/있다 takes 에.

choose.en: At what time shall we meet?
choose.why: A specific time of an event takes the time marker 에.

choose.en: The wallet is inside the bag.
choose.why: Static location where an object exists takes 에.

choose.en: I am at home on Sunday.
choose.why: Both the time (일요일) and the static existence place (집) take 에.

cards.when: 가다, 오다와 함께 목적지를 나타낼 때
cards.en: I go to school every morning.

cards.when: 집이나 고향으로 돌아올 때
cards.en: I came home in the evening.

cards.when: 수량이나 개수당 기준을 말할 때
cards.en: Apples are 1,000 won each.

cards.when: 하루나 일주일 동안 몇 번 하는지 셀 때
cards.en: I drink water often in a day.

split.en: Minsu went to the park.
Sujin comes to the company.
Watermelon is 10,000 won for one.
I read three books in a week.

choose.en: Where are you going? I drop by the market.
choose.why: Destination with movement takes the direction marker 에.

choose.en: Eggs are 3,000 won for ten.
choose.why: Marking price per unit of count takes 에.

choose.en: Jiyoung entered the library.
choose.why: Entering into a destination takes 에.

choose.en: I go to the hospital twice a day.
choose.why: The first 에 marks frequency per day, and the second marks hospital as destination.

cards.when: 무엇을 먹거나 배우는 구체적인 행동을 할 때
cards.en: I eat a meal at a restaurant.

cards.when: 도서관이나 회사에서 활동할 때
cards.en: I study for the exam at the library.

cards.when: 어디에서 출발하여 오는지 나타낼 때
cards.en: The plane came from America.

cards.when: 어느 나라나 고향에서 왔는지 소개할 때
cards.en: I came from Korea.

split.en: Minsu bought shoes at the market.
I met a friend at the cafe.
My younger sibling reads a book in the room.
I ran diligently in the park.

choose.en: Sujin watches a movie at the theater.
choose.why: The dynamic action of watching a movie at a location takes 에서.

choose.en: Where do you depart from? I depart from Seoul Station.
choose.why: Starting point of departure takes 에서.

choose.en: I borrowed a book at the library.
choose.why: Borrowing a book is an action that takes place at a location, taking 에서.

choose.en: I rest at home and drink coffee at a cafe.
choose.why: Both resting and drinking coffee are active events happening at locations, taking 에서.

fill.en: I bought bread at the bakery.

cards.when: 어디에서 시작하여 어디까지 가는지 거리를 말할 때
cards.en: I walk from home to work.

cards.when: 언제부터 언제까지 시간이 걸리는지 나타낼 때
cards.en: I work from nine o'clock to six o'clock.

cards.when: 월요일부터 금요일처럼 요일 범위를 말할 때
cards.en: There are classes from Monday to Friday.

cards.when: 한 도시에서 다른 도시까지 이동할 때
cards.en: I take a train from Seoul to Busan.

split.en: It takes ten minutes from my house to school.
I studied from one o'clock to three o'clock.
The festival is held from today to tomorrow.
I walked from the station to the park.

choose.en: We start the meeting from ten in the morning.
choose.why: Starting point in time takes 부터.

choose.q: 어디___ 어디까지 가요? 서울에서 대전까지 가요.
choose.en: From where to where are you going? From Seoul to Daejeon.
choose.why: Starting point in physical location takes 에서.

choose.en: I took a taxi from the airport to the hotel.
choose.why: The end destination point takes 까지.

choose.en: I take a rest from Wednesday to Thursday.
choose.why: A time span from Wednesday to Thursday uses the pair 부터 ~ 까지.

fill.en: I go from home to the market.
I am busy from morning to evening.

cards.when: 누구에게 선물이나 물건을 주는지 말할 때
cards.en: I gave a birthday present to my sibling.

cards.when: 누구에게 말을 하거나 묻는지 나타낼 때
cards.en: I told a secret to my friend.

cards.when: 전화나 편지를 보내는 대상을 가리킬 때
cards.en: I made a phone call to Minsu.

cards.when: 학생이나 아이들에게 지식을 가르칠 때
cards.en: The teacher teaches a song to students.

split.en: Sujin sent a letter to a friend.
I gave water to the puppy.
Minsu asked Jiyoung.
I waved my hand to older brother.

choose.en: I gave bread to my friend.
choose.why: Giving something to a person in conversational Korean takes 한테.

choose.en: Please ask Jiyoung.
choose.why: Directing an inquiry to a person takes 한테.

choose.en: I gave candy to my younger sibling.
choose.why: The person receiving the candy takes 한테.

choose.en: Minsu presented flowers to Jiyoung.
choose.why: Subject 민수 takes 가, and recipient 지영 takes 한테.

fill.en: I gave a book to Minsu.
I wrote a letter to older sister.

cards.when: 두 가지 이상의 물건을 대등하게 묶을 때
cards.en: There are apples and pears on the table.

cards.when: 누구와 같이 어떤 행동을 하는지 말할 때
cards.en: I watch a movie with a friend on the weekend.

cards.when: 말할 때 자연스럽게 사물이나 사람을 이을 때
cards.en: I bought bread and milk.

cards.when: 같거나 다름을 견주는 상대를 가리킬 때
cards.ko: 이 옷은 형 옷{과} 색이 같아요.
cards.en: This outfit has the same color as older brother's clothes.

split.en: Minsu walks in the park with a friend.
I drank coffee and water.
I had a chat with Jiyoung.
I bought a notebook and a pencil.

choose.en: I bought watermelon and bananas.
choose.why: 수박 ends in a consonant, so 과.

choose.en: Older brother and younger sibling laugh.
choose.why: 형 ends in a consonant, so 이랑.

choose.en: I played together with my friend on the weekend.
choose.why: Doing an action together with a friend takes 하고.

choose.en: Apples and strawberries, hat and bag.
choose.why: Both 사과 and 모자 end in vowels, so both take 와.

cards.when: 앞 사람의 말에 나도 그렇다고 덧붙일 때
cards.en: I am a student too.

cards.when: 한 가지 외에 다른 것도 더할 때
cards.en: I ate an apple, and I ate a banana too.

cards.when: 다른 사람이나 대상도 같은 행동을 할 때
cards.en: Minsu goes, and Jiyoung goes too.

cards.when: 두 가지 좋은 점을 함께 말할 때
cards.ko: 이 식당은 맛{도} 좋고 값{도} 싸요.
cards.en: This restaurant has good taste and the price is cheap too.

split.en: I like coffee too.
Minsu eats bread too.
Today is warm too.
My younger sibling is kind too.

choose.en: I learn Korean too.
choose.why: Expressing 'me too' takes 도.

choose.en: I sing and dance too.
choose.why: Adding dancing to singing takes 도.

choose.en: Apples are delicious. Strawberries are sweet too.
choose.why: Saying strawberries are sweet as well takes 도.

choose.en: Sujin comes, and Minsu came too.
choose.why: Both Sujin and Minsu coming takes 도 · 도.

cards.when: 다른 것은 빼고 오직 그것 하나만 가리킬 때
cards.en: Only Minsu is in the classroom.

cards.when: 여러 음식 중 한 가지만 고를 때
cards.en: I eat only apples.

cards.when: 조금만 기다려 달라고 부탁할 때
cards.en: Please wait for just five minutes.

cards.when: 다른 사람에게는 비밀로 하고 한 사람에게만 말할 때
cards.en: I will tell only you.

split.en: Only Sujin came to the park.
I drank only water today.
Please give me just one.
My younger sibling reads only comic books.

choose.q: 다른 친구는 안 오고 지영이___ 왔어요.
choose.en: Other friends did not come and only Jiyoung came.
choose.why: Only Jiyoung came, excluding others, so 만.

choose.en: I want to rest just a little.
choose.why: Wanting to rest 'just a little' takes 만.

choose.en: I do not eat meat and eat only vegetables.
choose.why: Eating only vegetables exclusively takes 만.

choose.q: 저는 커피___ 마시고 차는 안 마셔요.
choose.en: I drink only coffee, not tea.
choose.why: 만 means only: coffee and nothing else.

cards.when: 남은 것이 너무 적어서 부족하다고 느낄 때
cards.en: There is nothing but a glass of water.

cards.when: 남은 개수가 하나뿐일 때
cards.en: Only one apple is left.

cards.when: 가진 돈이 너무 모자랄 때
cards.en: I have nothing but 1,000 won in my wallet.

cards.when: 의지할 사람이 오직 한 사람뿐일 때
cards.en: I have nobody but my friend.

split.en: There is only ten minutes left.
There are only two coins in the pocket.
Only three people came to the classroom.
I know only Korean.

choose.en: Only one apple is left.
choose.why: With negative 안 남았어요 expressing shortage, use 밖에.

choose.en: I could only sleep for two hours.
choose.why: With negative verb 못 잤어요 expressing insufficient sleep, use 밖에.

choose.en: I have only 1,000 won in my wallet.
choose.why: With negative 없어요 expressing shortage of money, use 밖에.

choose.q: 교실에 지영 씨___ 민수 씨___ 안 남았어요.
choose.en: In the classroom, only Jiyoung and Minsu are left.
choose.why: Connecting two people with 하고 and expressing scarcity with negative 안 남았어요 takes 하고 · 밖에.

fill.en: I could read only three pages.

cards.when: 둘 중 아무거나 먹고 싶을 때
cards.en: I eat bread or rice.

cards.when: 상대방에게 차나 음료를 권할 때
cards.en: Drink coffee or tea.

cards.when: 약속 날짜를 둘 중 하나로 정할 때
cards.en: Let's meet on Saturday or Sunday.

cards.when: 마땅한 것이 없어 차선책을 고를 때
cards.en: I am bored, shall we watch a movie or something?

split.en: I read a book or newspaper in the morning.
Eat apples or bananas.
I ride a bus or subway.
Sujin went to the market or supermarket.

choose.en: I eat watermelon or Korean melon.
choose.why: 수박 ends in a consonant, so 이나.

choose.en: I drink milk or juice.
choose.why: 우유 ends in a vowel, so 나.

choose.en: Shall we go hiking or something on the weekend?
choose.why: Suggesting an activity casually as an option takes 이나.

choose.en: Wallets or bags, hats or shoes.
choose.why: 지갑 ends in a consonant (이나) and 모자 ends in a vowel (나).

fill.en: Let's watch a movie or something.

cards.when: 먹은 양이 생각보다 많아 놀랄 때
cards.en: I ate as many as three bowls of rice.

cards.when: 모인 사람이 기대보다 훨씬 많을 때
cards.en: As many as ten guests came.

cards.when: 걸린 시간이 너무 길다고 느낄 때
cards.en: I waited for my friend for as long as two hours.

cards.when: 물건값이 예상보다 지나치게 비쌀 때
cards.ko: 사과가 한 개에 오천 원{이나} 해요.
cards.en: Apples cost as much as 5,000 won each.

split.en: Minsu drank as many as four cups of coffee.
Sujin read as many as five books today.
split.ko: 수진은 오늘 책 다섯 권이나 읽었어요.

split.en: I walked as many as ten kilometers in the park.
There are as many as twenty students in the classroom.

choose.en: I bought as many as five apples!
choose.why: 개 ends in a vowel, so 나.

choose.en: I ate as many as seven candies!
choose.why: 알 ends in a consonant, so 이나.

choose.en: I have as much as 100,000 won!
choose.why: Expressing surprise at an unexpectedly large amount takes 이나.

choose.q: 세 잔___ 마시고 두 시간___ 잤어요.
choose.en: I drank as many as three cups and slept for as long as two hours.
choose.why: 잔 and 시간 both end in consonants, taking 이나 · 이나.

fill.en: I ate as many as three.
It takes as long as five hours.
As many as fifty people gathered.

cards.when: 버스나 지하철을 타고 이동할 때
cards.en: I go to school by bus.

cards.when: 어느 언어로 대화하는지 나타낼 때
cards.en: I talk with a friend in Korean.

cards.when: 오른쪽이나 위쪽으로 향할 때
cards.en: Please go to the right.

cards.when: 무엇으로 만들었는지 재료를 밝힐 때
cards.en: I made a chair with wood.

split.en: I write a letter with a pen.
Minsu goes to Seoul by train.
Please come forward slowly.
I cut paper with scissors.

choose.en: I write letters with a pencil.
choose.why: 연필 ends in the consonant ㄹ, so it takes 로.

choose.en: I eat rice with my hands.
choose.why: 손 ends in a consonant other than ㄹ, so 으로.

choose.en: I transfer by subway.
choose.why: Transportation method takes 로.

choose.en: I go by taxi and come by bus.
choose.why: Both 택시 and 버스 end in vowels, taking 로.

cards.when: 정확하지 않고 대략적인 시간을 잡을 때
cards.en: Let's meet around three o'clock.

cards.when: 대략적인 가격을 짐작하여 말할 때
cards.en: It costs about 5,000 won.

cards.when: 물건이나 과일 개수를 어림할 때
cards.en: I bought about five apples.

cards.when: 사람 수를 대략 짐작할 때
cards.en: About twenty people gathered in the playground.

split.en: It takes about thirty minutes from home to school.
Minsu will arrive around two o'clock.
About ten students are in the library.
I read about half of this book.

choose.q: 몇 시___ 만날까요? 한 시쯤 만나요.
choose.en: Around what time shall we meet? Let's meet around one.
choose.why: Asking or stating approximate time takes 쯤.

choose.en: This outfit costs about 10,000 won.
choose.why: Approximating price takes 쯤.

choose.en: Please give me about three apples.
choose.why: Requesting an approximate quantity takes 쯤.

choose.en: Around four o'clock, about five people gather.
choose.why: Both approximate time and headcount take 쯤.

cards.when: 하얗거나 둥근 모양이 비슷할 때
cards.en: The skin is white like snow.

cards.when: 마음이나 장소가 바다처럼 넓을 때
cards.en: The heart is wide like the sea.

cards.when: 선생님이나 부모님을 닮고 싶을 때
cards.en: I want to become a kind person like my teacher.

cards.when: 봄날처럼 따스하고 포근할 때
cards.en: The smile is warm like a spring day.

split.en: Minsu runs fast like a cheetah.
Sujin sings well like a singer.
Water is clear like glass.
The child laughs brightly like an angel.

choose.en: Flowers white like snow bloomed.
choose.why: Resembling snow in whiteness takes 처럼.

choose.en: I look at the sky blue like the sea.
choose.why: Resembling the sea takes 같이.

choose.en: My younger sibling hops like a rabbit.
choose.why: Comparing jumping action to a rabbit takes 처럼.

choose.en: Clear like water and shining like stars.
choose.why: Both comparing resemblance to water and stars take 처럼.

fill.en: She is kind like an angel.
It is wide like the sea.

cards.when: 둘 중 무엇이 더 큰지 견줄 때
cards.en: Watermelons are bigger than apples.

cards.when: 비행기와 기차의 빠르기를 비교할 때
cards.en: Airplanes are faster than trains.

cards.when: 사람의 키나 신체를 견줄 때
cards.en: My older brother is taller than me.

cards.when: 어제와 오늘의 기온을 비교할 때
cards.en: Today is colder than yesterday.

split.en: Trains are faster than buses.
Minsu is bigger than me.
Summer is hotter than spring.
Apples are sweeter than lemons.

choose.en: Older brother is taller than younger sibling.
choose.why: Comparing height against younger sibling takes 보다.

choose.en: Airplanes are much faster than ships.
choose.why: Comparing speed against a ship takes 보다.

choose.en: Today is busier than yesterday.
choose.why: Comparing today's busyness against yesterday takes 보다.

rule.ko: 「누가 · 뭐가」로 물으면 이/가로 답해요. 이미 알고 있는 것을 말하거나 둘을 견주면 은/는.
rule.en: A who/what question is answered with 이/가. Use 은/는 for what is already known, or to contrast two things.

situations.why: A who-question is answered with 이/가.
Something you just noticed takes 이/가.
